scenes.transcript: >> Um, of course, Genie can only learn from the data that it can actually reach. So it's important to talk a little bit about how Genie also gets access to this data that it's going to make sense of. Uh, we already have text to SQL, uh, which covers structured data that's governed in Unity Catalog. And I don't want to underestimate how much that matters. You know, a lot of agents are just reciting information that lives in a document. But when you're asking questions about your business, there often already isn't already a document that can answer those questions. That's why you're That's why you're asking. So, Genie is not only doing search, but also querying based on your live operational data. And we have dozens of connectors for that. Plus, actually Josh inspired uh a product that we call custom connectors um that allow the community connectors, sorry. Uh that allows you to create a connector to any generic uh application. So, thank you Josh actually for that idea. That That went straight into the product. Um for data that lives in in third-party applications, maybe that you want to query live instead of pulling it in and running that text to SQL, we also have uh MCP connectors. Again, they query live. So, you're getting things like the status of a Jira ticket, uh the status of a lead in Salesforce. It's really good for things like that. Uh we have, you know, maybe a dozen a dozen plus um of those MCP connectors. You can hook up a custom connector, and we're planning to to add quite a bit more here. But, when you want to ask a question across a much larger volume of data um or across a lot of sources at once, a bit of a harder question, you need a little bit more horsepower than MCP. Uh and that's what we're building with the search index. It retrieves and ranks everything together instead of leaning on each provider's siloed search capabilities. And it also feeds the ontology. Uh so, we are ensuring that your your tickets and your wikis, whatever it may be, become part of Genie's context. And just as importantly, we enforce the the sources' permissions. So, for example, you're not seeing emails in Genie that you don't actually have access to in your inbox. And that's a big deal because recreating source permissions in Unity Catalog is a is a pretty hard problem.
